text: PERFORMANCE & STABILITY Given the aforementioned stock experience, I found performance to be excellent. While forums are littered with reports of glitches, crashes, and other issues, I’ve found no such issues. Once again, it’s worth highlighting that Essential has released countless updates in effort to get to this point; which it should have been at launch. I’ve had no force closes, no stuttering, no unusual input lag, wobble, etc. If you look close enough, you can find a problem with any phone. Watching very closely, I can see the screen doesn’t respond 100% in sync with my input. However, when compared side-by-side with my Galaxy S8 Plus, it’s virtually identical in terms of responsiveness when scrolling. Except that in daily usage, it’s very clear stock android is still noticeably smoother than TouchWiz. I don’t have a Google phone handy, but from previous experience, it’s certainly on-par.

4. The Camera is amazing in well-lit condition but it does suffer a bit in low-light condition, but use a flash - it's acceptable. The portrait mode is amazing! Install the Google Camera apk and you'd have a different breed of camera UI and performance. 5. Performance and response are still surprisingly fast. I remember my old Android phones that after several months it started to bog down and almost to the point of being unresponsive; not this phone. I've only had to restore it once since I've owned, but that is to my fault. 6. Stock and Developer options! For those power users, this is a good option to have. 7. Battery still holds a charge quite well. I did install MacroDroid to control some applications and events as it seems that when I'm home, my battery depletes faster than when I'm out and about.

Very slow restart. - Poor touch responsiveness. Noticeable delay between touch and screen response. This gets worse towards the edges of the screen. - If you play games (ex. PUBG), you will notice lagging or non-responsiveness (really annoying) to touch pretty frequently. The phone will heat up fast and stay hot for a duration of time due to its build. - Reception is really bad. Same location, room, and carrier, but I get about half the signal my friends with galaxy or iphones get. At times, my friends can call or text, but I can't cause I have no signal when we are in a building. Rarely get full signal even outside in downtown of a major city where my carrier has dominance in the area... **My #1 complaint about the phone.** - Wifi signal is weak.

I use a case when I am out and about, but I take it off while at home or work just to enjoy the feel of this phone. The smoothness of the titanium and ceramic coupled with the added weight of the phone make it feel special. Even the haptic feedback feels better than in other devices I've used. The vibrations are audible in silent rooms, but it has a great feel to it. Many of my friends with other Android phones like the feel so much that they will play with my phone just to feel the haptic feedback. It's small things like this that make the Essential phone truly enjoyable to use. +The Camera - While this phone started off with terrible camera performance, the many updates to the camera app have caused me to truly enjoy taking pictures.

I went over 24-hours without charging at one point and wound up with 45%. It would have long been dead if it had been my Nokia. This was after the latest OS update (again, see below), so this might have been a factor in the longevity. Performance: I have absolutely no complaints here so far. There's no bloatware and the Oreo update took about an hour, overall (including the download.) I know there were several complaints about OS behavior, et al, pertaining to what was initially released on the phone. As I waited until all the updates were done before doing anything on the phone, I probably saved myself from a number of disappointments. At this point, the phone is fast and responsive, both within applications and switching between multiple applications. More evaluation will be required here but I'm satisfied so far.

The Key2 was my number 1, but my budget wouldn't allow for it or the Galaxy S9. The Essential Phone has a large, beautiful screen in a diminutive chassis that is smaller and slightly heavier than my 6S Plus. The screen is extremely responsive, and feels great. It also has force feedback during typing, which I find helpful and sorely lacking on the iPhones. I couldn't type on my 6S Plus without wanting to punch it repeatedly in frustration due to all the input lag and typos. My typing on the Essential Phone is hyper-accurate, and the autocorrect is not overly ambitious. Unlike the iPhone, the Essential's autocorrect doesn't just assume that every word I type is somehow wrong. The rest of the Essential Phone is just as gorgeous as the screen.

It was all okay with some hiccups every now and then, I knew that before getting it but I believed in Essential team's frequent updates. The most things that frustrated me were random shutdowns, most of apps are not (yet) compatible with the notch, the slow response of Google Assistant and the shutter lag of the camera (though quality of photos taken were very good). Anyway, in mid-March my phone couldn't turn on the screen. Did a restart, hard reset, power off/on but the device didn't seem to respond nor reviving the screen. Phone seemed to be dead, screen was only able to illuminates blacks when turned on. I was getting accurate vibration feedback form the fingerprint scanner (long vibration for registered fingers/ two short ones for other fingers) and from power off/on.

Screen is not as responsive as I'd expected.. Ok so I've had it a few days now. Positives: Pretty fast. Battery is ok so far. Lots of space! 24% of the memory used with all of my previous apps ported over. Super fast wi-fi. CONS: I've noticed the screen jittery thing going on, and the speaker is kind of muffled since it comes out the bottom. The biggest thing I have noticed is (and this is before I have added a screen protector) is the edges of the screen are not very responsive. If you are playing a game on the phone, the very edges of the screen take a few taps to register. The screen is also smaller than my Samsung J7 which I paid $150 for.

Other than that however I had no issues. So gaming on this device was really really good top notch. 11. Benchmarks- now this is going to be a real quick category in terms of events marks again we're running the Snapdragon 835 processor and the Adreno 540 GPU which was last year's flagship chipset so the benchmarks performed pretty much where I was expecting them to off the charts if not some of the highest benchmarks that I've seen in awhile. But what I want to emphasize here is benchmarks nowadays mean absolutely nothing what I feel like everyone should be looking out for is the right combination of hardware and software which equates to an overall smooth and fluid user experience. Which equals a good user experience at the end of the day. Which I feel this device delivers in spades.

It provides an excellent approach to giving a user access to exactly what .... Unlike most phones today, this one is not self serving. It provides an excellent approach to giving a user access to exactly what they want not what it wants. No bloatware and excessive advertising through applications you do not want. It is a very clean, fast and high quality product. Hopefully the company will continue its product line utilizing the same approach it has started with. Even though it has impressive technical specs, I believe there are many of us out here who will appreciate it for it's understated elegance even more. Good job guys, keep up the good work.
